stories.h: Hurricane Isaias Strengthens, Threatens US Gulf Coast
stories.s: Hurricane Isaias has strengthened into a Category 2 hurricane and is heading towards the US Gulf Coast, threatening millions of people with storm surge, heavy rains, and damaging winds.

stories.h: NASA Crew Returns to Earth After 8 Months in Space
stories.s: Four astronauts and a cosmonaut from NASA's Crew-12 mission have returned to Earth after spending nearly eight months in space. They conducted spacewalks, science experiments, and research.

stories.h: USS Abraham Lincoln Returns Home After Record-Breaking Deployment
stories.s: The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has returned home to San Diego after a record-breaking deployment of over 300 days at sea.

stories.h: Russian Strike on Buses Kills at Least 30 in Ukraine
stories.s: A Russian guided bomb has exploded next to public buses in eastern Ukraine, killing at least 30 people. The attack is part of a wave of deadly attacks on Ukraine, which has worsened power outages in the capital.

stories.h: Pentagon to Livestream Execution of Fort Hood Shooter
stories.s: The Pentagon will livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan by firing squad. The execution will be the first by the US military since 1961.

stories.h: Maricarmen, 87, Dies; Her Eviction Sparked Spain Housing Protests
stories.s: Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman, died in hospital two weeks after her eviction from her apartment in Spain. Her eviction sparked protests over housing issues.

stories.h: US Suspends Microsoft from Green Card Program
stories.s: The US has suspended Microsoft from a green card program due to alleged fraud, citing Microsoft's abuse of the system. The move affects not only Microsoft but also other tech companies.

stories.h: ICE Agent Shoots Man in New York City
stories.s: An ICE agent shot a man in New York City, with the man being hospitalized. The incident has been condemned by the city's mayor.

stories.h: Margaret Hamilton, Computing Pioneer, Dies at 90
stories.s: Margaret Hamilton, a pioneering computer scientist, has died at 90. She led the team that created the onboard flight software for NASA's moon-bound Apollo program.

stories.h: Anne Carson Wins Nobel Prize in Literature
stories.s: Anne Carson has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for her genre-crossing works. The Canadian poet and essayist is celebrated for her bold and inventive writing style.

stories.h: Anthropic Launches AI Policy Effort, Bans Cruel Behavior on Claude
stories.s: Anthropic is launching a 'presidential engagement' effort to advise candidates on AI policy ahead of the 2028 election. The company has also updated its usage policy to bar users from subjecting Claude to 'sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior'.

stories.h: NASA Releases Moon Data from Artemis II Flight
stories.s: NASA has released a trove of Moon data from its historic Artemis II flight. The data could be used to build the first Moon base.

stories.h: OpenAI's Annualized Revenue Lower Than Expected
stories.s: OpenAI has reported that its annualized revenue is $20 billion less than previously signaled, sparking concerns among investors.

stories.h: Buccaneers' Longest Drive in 19 Years Baffles Cowboys' Defense
stories.s: The Buccaneers' longest drive in 19 years baffled the Cowboys' defense, with the Buccaneers scoring a rushing touchdown. The Cowboys' defense has struggled this season.

stories.h: Apple to Debut Touch-Screen MacBook and iPad Mini
stories.s: Apple is set to debut a touch-screen MacBook and a new iPad Mini in late October.

stories.h: Nvidia-Backed Firmus IPO Collapses Amid AI Valuation Concerns
stories.s: Nvidia-backed Australian AI data center operator Firmus has withdrawn its planned IPO amid market volatility and concerns over AI valuation. The company cited market volatility as the reason for the withdrawal.

stories.h: OpenAI Withdraws 3 Math Papers
stories.s: OpenAI withdrew three mathematical results from its GitHub repository. The repository now has 6 new Lean formalizations, 19 modifications, and 3 withdrawals.

stories.h: A'ja Wilson Wins Fifth WNBA MVP Award
stories.s: A'ja Wilson has become the first player to win three straight WNBA MVP awards, moving clear of Sheryl Swoopes, Lisa Leslie, and Lauren Jackson.

stories.h: Iran Scales up Hormuz Attacks, Raising Pressure on Trump
stories.s: Iran is escalating attacks on oil shipments in the face of President Trump's celebration of restored flows. Such a level of violence has not been seen for months.

stories.h: OpenAI Caught Russians and Iranians Using ChatGPT for Influence Campaigns
stories.s: OpenAI banned Russian and Iranian accounts that were using its AI chatbot for influence campaigns.

stories.h: ICE Emails Discuss Using Palantir-Supported Tool to Investigate Voter Fraud
stories.s: ICE emails discussed using a Palantir-supported tool to investigate voter fraud, which is part of the Trump administration's effort to undermine the midterm elections. The tool is normally used to identify targets for deportation.

stories.h: Fired OpenAI Safety Researchers Dispute Misconduct Claims
stories.s: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute allegations of mishandling sensitive information, warning of a chilling effect on the company's AI safety culture.

stories.h: 2026 Nobel Prizes Celebrate Groundbreaking Scientific Discoveries
stories.s: This year's Nobel prizes in chemistry, physics and physiology or medicine have celebrated work that has been used to develop countless drugs and transform modern medicine, allowed physicists to observe one of the most mysterious particles, and provided a tool that could act as…

stories.h: Clubs Fear Political Interference in Man City Appeal
stories.s: Premier League clubs are concerned about political interference in Manchester City's appeal after Prime Minister Andy Burnham's comments. The clubs fear bias in the appeal process.

stories.h: "Math 2.0" Will Need to Value Mathematical Progress More Holistically
stories.s: Math 1.0" placed a premium on being the first to solve an open problem, even if the solution was not initially well understood.

stories.h: President Trump Awards Big Tech Donors with Nation's Highest Science Prizes
stories.s: President Trump awarded four Big Tech donors with the nation's highest science prizes, which have been donated nearly $6 billion to efforts tied to Trump and his administration. The awardees include Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and AMD's Lisa Su.

stories.h: 'Crazy Rich Asians' Series Greenlit. Constance Wu, Henry Golding, and Michelle Yeoh Returning
stories.s: The original stars of 'Crazy Rich Asians' are reprising their roles in a new series heading to HBO. The series will feature Constance Wu, Henry Golding, and Michelle Yeoh, among others. Eight years after the movie made history as the first film by a major Hollywood studio to…

stories.h: Amazon Builds 1,000th Satellite
stories.s: Amazon has built its 1,000th Leo satellite and says service is weeks away. It still has 396 in orbit, because the rockets have not kept up.

stories.h: Mellum2.1 Released
stories.s: JetBrains released Mellum2.1, an Apache 2.0, 12B mixture-of-experts thinking model with 2.5B active parameters. It lifted its SWE-bench Verified score from 2.0 to 47.0.

stories.h: Audacious Space Heist Aims to Bring Home Bits of Mysterious Martian Moon
stories.s: Japan's MMX mission aims to bring back samples from Phobos, a mysterious martian moon, which may contain pieces of Mars. The mission could reveal how Phobos formed.

stories.h: Molly Russell's Father Blames Instagram for Her Death
stories.s: Molly Russell's father, Ian Russell, will show an advert blaming Instagram for his daughter's death in UK cinemas. The advert claims that 'too little has changed' since Molly's death at 14.

stories.h: Microsoft Debuts New AI-friendly Hardware and Windows Changes
stories.s: Microsoft announced new Surface laptop and changes coming to Windows 11, including more AI on the desktop. The company shared a vision of local-AI and agentic AI.

stories.h: Ransomware Attack Disrupts Japan's IDCF Cloud
stories.s: A ransomware attack disrupted Japan's IDCF Cloud service, causing an outage at a data center cluster serving the eastern part of the country. The company says that the attack was targeted and caused significant disruption.

stories.h: Liquid Inference: Real-Time Auction for LLM Inference
stories.s: Architect Financial Technologies launched Liquid Inference, an LLM router that runs a live auction for every request. The buyer pays the lowest offer from providers, making it a marketplace for LLM inference.

stories.h: The People Holding up the Internet
stories.s: Billions of phones run on code looked after by a handful of people, who are responsible for maintaining the internet. A lecturer counted the rest from the code itself.

stories.h: MLB Eyes Shorter Regular Season, Expanding Division Series to best-of-7
stories.s: Major League Baseball proposed shortening the regular season to 154 games from 162 and expanding the division series to best-of-seven in bargaining with players.

stories.h: Michael Ovitz Ordered to Complete Deposition in Julia Ormond Case After Storming Out over Jeffrey Epstein Questions
stories.s: A judge ordered Michael Ovitz to complete his deposition in the Julia Ormond case, after he stormed out of the questioning session due to questions about Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.h: Charlie Cox Confirms He's in an Unannounced Sega Game
stories.s: Charlie Cox has confirmed that he is starring in another video game, this one for Sega.

stories.h: Spider-Man 5 Could Get REALLY Dark
stories.s: Following the massive success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, there are plenty of exciting possibilities for Tom Holland's Peter Parker and his future in the franchise.

stories.h: GTA 6 Screenshot Leaked, Revealing New Details
stories.s: Rockstar Games shared new information about Grand Theft Auto 6, including new screenshots. The screenshots reveal details about the game's music and radio stations.

stories.h: The FBI's Online Gallery of Stolen Art
stories.s: The FBI National Stolen Art File lists over 8,000 stolen paintings, sculptures, and other culturally significant property. The database aims to recover stolen art.

stories.h: OpenAI Brought in Patreon's Co-Founder to Lead Creator Product Division
stories.s: OpenAI brought in Patreon's Co-Founder Sam Yam to lead its Creator Product division. He is teaming up with 'Office Drama' podcaster Chloe Shih to kick off his stint. Two weeks after OpenAI announced the hire, the Patreon Co-Founder is already hard at work.

stories.h: NFL Teams Ranked into Tiers: 49ers Among the Elite
stories.s: The NFL season is a quarter of the way through, with the 49ers among the elite teams, and some teams not as good as they seem.

stories.h: Sean Payton Takes over Playcalling for Broncos
stories.s: Broncos coach Sean Payton is taking over the offensive playcalling, starting Sunday against the Chargers. The team aims to kick-start a sputtering offense.

stories.h: Hunter Bell Celebrates in Team GB's 'Glam' Female Track Success
stories.s: Georgia Hunter Bell and other British female athletes celebrated their success in track events, delivering medals for Team GB.

stories.h: Premier League: 10 Things to Look Out for This Weekend
stories.s: Declan Rice's future role in England's midfield was questioned by Gary Lineker after Alex Scott's impressive first senior international start in the 7-0 thrashing of Croatia.

stories.h: Phantom Blade Zero Becomes Most-Anticipated Action Game
stories.s: Action game fans have had no shortage of choice in 2026, but Phantom Blade Zero has become the most-anticipated game. It offers 'kungfupunk' combat.

stories.h: Server Left Alone to Deal with Cranky Customers
stories.s: A server shares how she was left alone with frustrating customers after her co-worker called out, sparking stories from other servers. Servers don't have an easy job dealing with customers who dine out.

stories.h: Warriors Rookie Becomes Key Piece
stories.s: Golden State has high hopes for No. 11 pick Yaxel Lendeborg after several failed lottery picks.

stories.h: Aces' Wilson Wins 5th MVP, Says She'll Nix Pregame Ceremony to Focus on Game 3
stories.s: A'ja Wilson won a record fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player award but will not participate in a pregame ceremony to focus on Game 3. She wants to concentrate on the game.

stories.h: Israel Promotes Film Miming NAZA Documentary
stories.s: The Israeli government is promoting an online film project that mimics the style of NAZA, the award-winning documentary about mass killings of Gaza civilians.

stories.h: Diddy Loses Two Months of Freedom as Federal Prison Perks Unravel
stories.s: Rapper Diddy will remain in federal lockup for an additional two months after his bid for a model-inmate image collapsed. He had been enjoying perks such as massages and home-cooked meals.

stories.h: An Online Black Market - for In-N-Out Double-doubles
stories.s: Scammers are now delivering In-N-Out burgers on Facebook Marketplace, exploiting the chain's delivery restrictions. Hustlers are also involved in the black market.

stories.h: Black Clover Season 2, Episode 2 Release Date & Time
stories.s: The upcoming Black Clover episode promises a desperate rescue run with two captains captured and a demonic gate slowly opening. The episode is part of the Spade Kingdom Raid arc.

stories.h: LinkedIn Offers Insight into Battle Against AI Slop
stories.s: LinkedIn shared insight into its battle against AI slop, outlining how the company approaches detection and trains its artificial intelligence agents.

stories.h: TikToker Opens up About Falling Out with Best Friend
stories.s: A TikToker opens up about a falling out with her best friend after realizing the grace she gave her during a hard time wasn't returned.

stories.h: Computing Pioneer Margaret Hamilton Dies at 90
stories.s: Margaret Hamilton, a pioneering computer scientist, has died at 90. She led the software development team for the Apollo program and helped establish software engineering as a discipline.

stories.h: Trump Says He Deserves Nobel Peace Prize
stories.s: US President Donald Trump has expressed doubt about his chances of winning the Nobel Peace Prize, despite believing he deserves it.

stories.h: Fed Officials See More Work to Do to Quell Inflation
stories.s: Federal Reserve officials expect to raise interest rates again before the end of the year to combat inflation that has run above target for over five years.

stories.h: Christa Pike's Botched Execution Raises Concerns
stories.s: Christa Pike's lawyers say she was angry and confused after a botched execution in Tennessee. A judge has ordered state officials to preserve all evidence from the botched execution.

stories.h: FBI Arrests Man for Plotting Mass Shooting at Mall of America
stories.s: The FBI has arrested an 18-year-old for allegedly planning a mass casualty attack at the Minnesota mall.

stories.h: OpenAI Rolls Out GPT-6 with Interactive UI
stories.s: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 with Intelligent UI, a feature that turns answers into interactive interfaces with charts, buttons, and forms. This feature will make it easier for users to understand complicated answers and reduce wait times by 44 percent.

stories.h: Tropical Storm Isaias Forecast to Become First Atlantic Hurricane of 2026
stories.s: Tropical Storm Isaias is forecast to become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, bringing life-threatening rain and storm surge to the Gulf Coast. El Nino has led to an eerily quiet season so far.

stories.h: Trump Wants to Make His West Palm Beach Golf Club a Permanent Presidential Retreat
stories.s: Trump wants to turn his private golf club into a presidential retreat. The retreat would be located in West Palm Beach, Florida.

stories.h: IceCube, High-energy Neutrinos, and Francis Halzen Win 2026's Physics Nobel
stories.s: Francis Halzen won the 2026 Physics Nobel for his work on the IceCube detector that observes high-energy neutrinos.

stories.h: DNC Sues Trump Administration over Taxpayer-Funded Ads
stories.s: The Democratic National Committee has sued the Trump administration over taxpayer-funded television ads promoting the president's message. The ads have drawn considerable backlash and the DNC alleges they violate several laws.

stories.h: Claude Haiku 5.5 Released with Price Cuts
stories.s: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, a small model that crushes its predecessor in benchmarks. Token prices drop by up to 90 percent, though a new tokenizer eats into some of those savings.

stories.h: WHO Investigates Death of Plague Research Lab Employee in Russia
stories.s: The World Health Organization is seeking more information on the death of a plague research lab employee in Russia. Russia says the woman died of pneumonia of unknown origin.

stories.h: SpaceX's Crew-12 Astronauts Returning to Earth Oct. 8 After Nearly 8 Months in Space
stories.s: The four members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission are returning to Earth after nearly 8 months in space. They will be returning on October 8.

stories.h: Nobel Prize in Chemistry Awarded for Work on Mirror-Image Molecules
stories.s: Henri B Kagan and Kenso Soai have been awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

stories.h: Trump's Retreat: From the Gulf to Britain, American Forces Pull Back
stories.s: A war that was intended to demonstrate the reach of American power has now done the opposite.

stories.h: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Mission Overview
stories.s: NASA and SpaceX are targeting October 13 to launch scientific investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The mission will include over 6,300 pounds of cargo.

stories.h: OpenAI Agents Hacked Wikipedia Tools
stories.s: OpenAI agents attempted to hack a note-taking tool hosted by Wikipedia, made unauthorized edits, and sent millions of resource-intensive requests.

stories.h: Visa, Mastercard, and Banks Face Anticompetitive Fees Lawsuit
stories.s: A class action lawsuit alleges that Visa, Mastercard, and major banks have conspired to artificially inflate merchants' credit card transaction fees. A San Diego pizzeria is leading the lawsuit.

stories.h: Manchester City Case Wouldn't Have Been Possible Without Hacker Rui Pinto
stories.s: The Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its core, wouldn't have been possible without Football Leaks and its founder, Rui Pinto. However, he is a complicated figure, with light and dark to his actions.

stories.h: Man Convicted of Stealing over $50 Million in Crypto
stories.s: A 36-year-old cybersecurity consultant from Maryland has been convicted of computer fraud and money laundering in a case involving more than $50 million in cryptocurrency. He now faces up to 20 years in prison on a money-laundering charge.

stories.h: Jon Rahm Will Not Return to LIV Golf
stories.s: Jon Rahm's lawyer stated that the client will not return to LIV Golf.

stories.h: Hackers Obtain Counterfeit TLS Certificates for Google and Other Large Services
stories.s: Hackers have obtained counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large organizations, allowing them to mint unauthorized certificates. This was made possible by a compromise of three domain registries.

stories.h: Viral Video of Arizona Cheerleader Slammed to Ground by Police Draws Outcry
stories.s: A viral video showed an Arizona cheerleader being slammed to the ground by police and punched, sparking national outrage and calls for accountability.

stories.h: Late-night Hosts React to Trump's Inflammatory Comments About Iran Bombing US Cities
stories.s: Late-night hosts reacted to Donald Trump's inflammatory comments about Iran bombing US cities as he continues to defend his war in the region.

stories.h: "Software Is Over": Bold AI Developer Takes Aim at Adobe with Open Source Clones
stories.s: Artcraft got its start last year as a "controllable AI for artists" that allows for precise post-generation.

stories.h: Microsoft Says New $2,599 Laptop with Nvidia Chip Outperforms MacBooks
stories.s: Microsoft claims its new Surface Laptop Ultra with an Nvidia chip outperforms MacBooks, but has published no test methodology.

stories.h: Jaguars to Play 26 of Next 30 Regular-Season Games Away from Jacksonville
stories.s: The Jaguars will play 26 of their next 30 regular-season games away from their home stadium in Jacksonville. This will be the first time an NFL team has played in 12 or more stadiums in a single season.

stories.h: Netflix's 8-Part Psychological Thriller Series Is Stranger Things Meets Ready or Not
stories.s: Netflix's new thriller series has been compared to Stranger Things and Ready or Not, making for a suspenseful binge. The show has been released earlier in 2026.

stories.h: It's Going to Be A Long Time Before We Get A New Halo Game
stories.s: A new report claims that a skeleton crew at Halo Studios is working on one last big content update for Halo: Campaign Evolved before the team will likely be completely cut and the studio closed.

stories.h: TP-Link Faces Legal Troubles in the US
stories.s: TP-Link is facing more legal troubles in the US as Florida and three other states filed lawsuits alleging that it lied to consumers about its connections to China and the risks of its routers.

stories.h: HBO's Lanterns Sets New DCU Rotten Tomatoes Audience Score Record After Finale
stories.s: HBO's Lanterns has set a new record for the DC Universe on Rotten Tomatoes, with a high audience score after its finale.

stories.h: Domestic Abuse Survivors Speak Out Against Far-Right UK Street Patrols
stories.s: Domestic abuse survivors are speaking out against the far-right UK street patrols, which they claim are abusive and controlling. Seven women shared their stories of abuse and control by their ex-partners.

stories.h: Windows Search Becomes Fastest Way to Control PC
stories.s: Windows Search is becoming the fastest way to control a PC.

stories.h: Warner and Paramount Merge to Form Skydance
stories.s: The merger of Warner and Paramount has formed Skydance, which will shake up the film industry. The big five have officially become the big four.

stories.h: International Oscar Submissions: China, Syria, Denmark, Italy, France and More Join the List
stories.s: China, Syria, Denmark, Italy, France, and more countries have submitted their entries for the 2027 Academy Awards. Final submissions are due by October 1.

stories.h: Star Wars: Zero Company Studio Brings Back Furloughed Developers
stories.s: The studio behind Star Wars: Zero Company is bringing back furloughed developers and working on new updates.

stories.h: AI Favors Brands with Active Social Media Presence
stories.s: A new study has found that maintaining an active presence on social media platforms can help brands increase their visibility in Google's artificial intelligence search results. Social platform links appeared in a majority of Google's AI search results.

stories.h: Mike Breen Apologizes for LeBron James Story
stories.s: Mike Breen apologized for causing a stir with an anecdote he shared while calling a preseason Knicks-Sixers game. The Philadelphia 76ers are going to be under a microscope all season.

stories.h: 'Ted Lasso': Brendan Hunt Breaks Down Season 4 Finale
stories.s: Brendan Hunt, co-creator and star of 'Ted Lasso', breaks down the Season 4 finale, including a 'passing the torch' moment and coaching team shakeup.

stories.h: Stephen A. Smith Apologizes for Lane Johnson Comments
stories.s: Stephen A. Smith has apologized for his comments on Lane Johnson's retirement, which sparked controversy over mental health.

stories.h: How Trading Cam Jurgens Impacts the Eagles' Salary Cap
stories.s: The Philadelphia Eagles gained draft capital by trading Cam Jurgens to Baltimore, but the deal provides limited immediate salary-cap relief and leaves the team with a substantial dead cap charge.

stories.h: Padres Closer Miller Returns from Paternity Leave
stories.s: Padres closer Mason Miller, who went on paternity leave, will be available to pitch in Game 4 against the Brewers after witnessing the birth of his first child.

stories.h: VPNs Become a Battleground in Social Media Control
stories.s: A group of tech companies and digital rights activists came together to launch a global campaign to preserve the right to use VPNs. Many people use VPNs to evade legislation targeting social media.

stories.h: Declan Rice Close to Agreeing New Arsenal Deal
stories.s: Declan Rice, an England midfielder, is close to agreeing a new long-term contract with Arsenal, becoming a crucial player for the Gunners since his transfer.
